thread:
morgan: Heads up — big p99 regression on streaming after last night's rollout (release/1.12.0). p50 steady (~40ms) but p99 jumped from ~210ms to ~520ms. Grafana: https://grafana/redwood/dashboard/streaming :warning:

sam: Which surface? SSE, websocket, or both?

morgan: SSE only. Websocket traces look normal. Tool-calls (the /tool/** routes) are the worst hit. The spike aligns with the deploy time.

perf-ci: perf/streaming-end2end failed on master in CI at 2026-03-16T03:12Z — p99 latency 4.8x baseline, see artifact: https://ci.redwood/runs/7890

tia: I'll bisect now — git bisect start -- good v1.11.9 bad v1.12.0.

tia: bisect -> culprit commit: abc1234 (author: lucas) "coalesce small frames to reduce syscalls". Changes in stream_writer.cpp: introduced per-connection coalesce buffer + background timer flush (20ms).

lucas: yep that's mine. intent was to reduce syscall noise for many small tokens. I didn't realize the timer semantics would interact badly with tool-call serialization.

morgan: traces show ~18-22ms plateaus in tail latencies — consistent with a 20ms coalesce delay. Tool-call path creates nested frames that are queued until the coalesce flush runs, so multiple small waits accumulate.

sam: can we hotfix by disabling coalescing? feature flag?

lucas: pushed a canary config toggle and set `stream_coalesce=false` on canary. Command used: `cfg.set('stream_coalesce', false)` and deployed to canary cluster.

tia: canary metrics: p99 dropped from ~520ms to ~230ms, p50 unchanged. CI perf job retriggered and is green now.

morgan: awesome. creating a rollback PR to revert the coalescing change for the rollout: PR #4599 (revert abc1234) with revert commit def5678. This blocks the 1.12 rollout until merge.

lucas: FYI the allocation/batching side-effects: coalescing changed batching heuristics — we inadvertently made the runtime emit smaller kernel launches for some workloads because KV cache hits were now aligning differently in time. That likely amplified the tail. Follow-up needed on kernel-selection heuristics.

morgan: agree — short-term revert, long-term fix: selective coalescing (skip tool-call frames) + much smaller flush delay (2ms) + ensure coalesce doesn't change batching boundaries the scheduler uses.

lucas: opened follow-up PR #4600: "selective frame coalescing + coalesce_max_delay=2ms". Key diff (pseudocode):
```
if (coalesce && !is_tool_frame(payload)) {
  coalesce_buffer.append(payload);
  // flush timer: coalesce_max_delay (2ms)
} else {
  flush_immediately(payload);
}
```

sam: Nice. Add a perf-harness test that specifically exercises tool-call nested frames and KV cache alignment so we don't regress again.

tia: adding tests to perf-harness and a CI perf gate against p99 on streaming-tool scenario.

morgan: tagging @eng-sre and @eng-runtime. Rolling back in canary now, will promote once PR #4599 merges and CI green. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
